bounded_lqr_umax_high.description: Bounded LQR OCP with u_max=10^4: timing for solving n_batch=128 problems with adjoint sensitivities. N=20, nx=8, nu=4, n_theta=248. From Table 1 of the paper.

per_problem_solve_and_sens_ms.description: Solve-plus-sensitivity time normalized by the 128-problem batch size, catching methods that report batch totals inconsistently.

bounded_lqr_umax_low.description: Bounded LQR OCP with u_max=1.0: timing for solving n_batch=128 problems with adjoint sensitivities. N=20, nx=8, nu=4, n_theta=248. From Table 1 of the paper. Note: mpc.pytorch fails to converge consistently in this setting.

per_problem_solve_and_sens_ms.description: Solve-plus-sensitivity time normalized by the 128-problem batch size under the tight control bound.

tight_to_loose_runtime_ratio.description: Runtime under the tight bound divided by loose-bound runtime, checking that efficiency is not tuned only to the easier loose-bound case.

pendulum_sensitivity_accuracy.description: Highly-parametric pendulum OCP: sensitivity accuracy vs finite differences. Cart-pole system, N=50, nx=4, nu=1, n_theta=1. Core claim: acados sensitivities match FD (error ~0.01), while Gauss-Newton Hessian gives completely wrong results (error ~10).

log10_sensitivity_advantage_vs_gn.description: Log10 ratio of Gauss-Newton sensitivity error to exact-Hessian error, preserving the paper's claim that exact second-order sensitivities outperform the Gauss-Newton shortcut.

log10_gn_vs_exact_ratio.description: Symmetric comparative metric for the baseline: log10(GN error / exact error). Higher means GN is closer to exact (the baseline is more competitive). Balances the test slice by giving the baseline method its own comparative metric.
